Harbor Point Mutual Auto Insurance
Bodily Injury Unit
Claim Notes
Claim number:
C-1450
Claimant:
Crystal Yang
Adjuster:
Christopher Wong
February 11, 2025
Claim reported by phone. The claiamnt was driving a vehicle that struck another car while turning left at an
intersection. The policy driver is the claimant, and the policy is in force.
February 14, 2025
Spoke with the claimant, who is not represented by an attorney. The account of the turn and the impact was clear and
matched the first report.
February 15, 2025
Respnoding officer's report confirms the claimant was in the vehicle at the scene. The other driver's statement agrees
on the left turn and the point of impact.
March 7, 2025
Photographs taken at the scene show damage to the front corner and driver side. Some details in the photos line up
with the claimant's description, though the photos do not show the full sequence of events.
April 22, 2025
No independent witnesses to the collision have come forward. The only accounts so far are the claimant's, the other
driver's, and the officer's observations at the scene.
May 9, 2025
Claimant reports neck and lower back pain following the impact and has beugn treatment. The reported injury is
consistent with a collision of this type.
June 8, 2025
Medical records received. Treatment has continued somewhat longer than is typical for this kind of strain. No prior
injury to the same area appears in the records or in the claimant's history.
June 15, 2025
No earlier damage to the vehicle is on file. A neighbor mentioned seeing the car with damage some weeks before the
reported date, but has not provided details or a statement in writing.
June 30, 2025
Reviewed the damage estimate against the photos. It is not yet clear whether all of the listed damage resulted from
this impact or whether some of it was there before. Requested a repair inspection.
July 15, 2025
Claimant has repeated the same account of the collision in each conversation, including the timing, the direction of
travel, and the sequence of the turn.
September 7, 2025
File remains open pending the repair inspection, the complete medical records, and a decision on the neighbor's
information. Next review is scheduled once those items are in.
</page>

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page
says nothing about. The ratings are listed from least to most suspicious.
- injury_crash_fit: Does the claimed injury fit the type and force of the crash? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- treatment_growth: Did the treatment grow beyond what this injury needs? Allowed: Normal, Elevated, Disproportionate, Extreme.
- pre_existing_condition: Did an earlier condition of the same body area add to the complaints? Allowed: None, Minor, Material, Predominant.
- occurrence_support: Do independent sources (witnesses, photos, cameras, the other driver) confirm that the accident happened as described? Allowed: Confirmed, Partially corroborated, Uncorroborated, Contradicted, Suspected staged.
- damage_crash_fit: Does the vehicle damage fit the described impact? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- account_stability: Did the claimant's account of the accident stay the same over time? Allowed: Stable, Clarified, Materially changed.
- occupant_presence: Was the claimant really in the vehicle at the time of the crash? Allowed: Verified, Unclear, Added later, Not present.
- prior_damage_evidence: Is there evidence of vehicle damage from before this crash? Allowed: None, Possible, Documented, Material.
- known_loss_evidence: Is there evidence the damage existed or was known before the coverage started? Allowed: Weak, Moderate, Strong.
- driver_status: Is the driver of the insured vehicle on the policy? Allowed: Listed, Household, Unlisted, Excluded.

For each rated feature give:
- "rating": exactly one of the allowed ratings,
- "confidence": "High", "Medium" or "Low" (how clearly the page shows it),
- "quote": one or two sentences copied EXACTLY from the page that support the rating, with any
  spelling errors as they are,
- "reason": one short sentence.
